channel.title: World
channel.description: The Washington Post World section provides information and analysis of breaking world news stories. In addition to our world news and video, Post World News offers discussions and blogs on major international news and economic issues.

item.title: Canada announces retaliatory tariffs on U.S. products as trade war deepens
item.dc:creator: Riley Beggin
item.description: Canada announced new tariffs of up to 50 percent on hundreds of American goods in retaliation for U.S. tariffs that took effect last week. Starting Sept. 8, Canada will double tariffs on American steel and aluminum to 50 percent and impose tariffs on around 700 other products.

item.title: CIA director makes rare, unannounced visit to Moscow
item.dc:creator: Alex Horton, Michael Birnbaum, Warren Strobel, Joyce Lee
item.description: The trip came as Ukrainian forces have stepped up attacks deep inside Russia, including in the capital.

item.title: The U.S. and Canada are in a trade war. China aims to win it.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Yang
item.description: Beijing, seeking an advantage, casts itself as a global champion of free trade.

item.title: The U.S. is escalating its economic war on Iran. Here’s what that means.
item.dc:creator: Sammy Westfall, Joshua Yang
item.description: Iran’s top trade partners include China, Iraq, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates. But the Trump administration has not said who new sanctions would target, or how so.

item.title: Trump says U.S. could rename Lake Ontario as Lake America amid Canada trade war
item.dc:creator: Sammy Westfall
item.description: The president cited his tariff fight in a social media post, saying the United States doesn’t expect to be “doing much business with Ontario any longer.”

item.title: As U.S.-Canada tensions escalate, Republicans could face political consequences
item.dc:creator: Gregory S. Schneider, Praveena Somasundaram
item.description: The threat of higher prices for gas, cars, hockey sticks and more gave fresh life to Democratic arguments that the president is destabilizing the economy.

item.title: Canada’s Carney makes rare show of open defiance against Trump
item.dc:creator: Ellen Francis
item.description: The Canadian prime minister has said his government will match U.S. tariffs "dollar for dollar."

item.title: Bessent unveils sweeping new Iran sanctions but delays toughest blow
item.dc:creator: Riley Beggin, David J. Lynch, Aoife Walsh
item.description: The treasury secretary said Trump is contacting other world leaders to demand their support for the “economic asphyxiation” of the Iranian regime but he declined to say which countries and gave no deadline for action.

item.title: What’s happening between the U.S. and Canada
item.dc:creator: Amber Phillips
item.description: And what it could mean for the American economy.

item.title: U.S. withdraws from military exercises with South Korea set for next month
item.dc:creator: Sammy Westfall
item.description: The move comes as the Iran war strains U.S. military resources in Asia.

item.title: Trump announces tariffs on Canadian vehicles, steel in escalation of trade war
item.dc:creator: David J. Lynch
item.description: President Donald Trump offered no additional details about the levies, but he said they would take effect Jan. 1 — leaving time for the two sides to resume negotiations.
